The matching paper is [1], “Fast and Geometrically Grounded Lorentz Neural Networks,” by Robert van der Klis and coauthors. It directly addresses Lorentz neural networks and the Lorentz model of hyperbolic space, proposing a new Lorentz linear layer, Lorentzian activation functions, and a caching strategy to make the networks both geometrically faithful and computationally efficient [1].

The other papers are about different topics, such as Clifford algebra networks [2], quadratic neural networks [3, 4], neural operators [6, 7], learning dynamics and scaling laws [8, 9], and long-horizon dynamical prediction [10].
